title: Gemini Live’s camera just became much more useful for accessibility
summary: Gemini can now describe your surroundings and guide your camera with spoken cues.
body: TL;DR Google is rolling out Guided Vision in Gemini Live for blind and low-vision users. Gemini can describe what the camera sees and verbally guide users to reframe the shot when needed. Guided Vision works on Android 9 and newer in markets that support Gemini Live. For blind and low-vision users, pointing a phone camera at something is only useful if the phone can explain what it sees. Google has been building towards just that with Gemini Live for more than a year, first adding visual guidance that could highlight objects on-screen . And now the company is turning that idea into a more accessibility-focused tool called Guided Vision. Guided Vision is rolling out today in Gemini Live on compatible Android phones. Once enabled, users can share their camera and hear real-time descriptions of what’s around them, ask follow-up questions, and get spoken instructions to adjust the camera. If Gemini needs a better view, for example, it can ask you to pan right, tilt down, or step back.

title: Google’s new Android sideloading rules are live — and here are all the ways to already bypass them
summary: From Advanced Flow to ADB and Shizuku, power users can continue installing unverified APKs on Android.
body: Credit: Megan Ellis / Android Authority TL;DR Certified Android devices running Google Play Services in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand now actively block apps from unverified developers, with a global rollout set for 2027. Users can bypass restrictions via Google’s multi-step “Advanced Flow” (which requires toggling Developer Options, restarting, waiting 24 hours, and a few more taps), ADB, Shizuku, rooting, or by using custom ROMs (like Lineage OS and GrapheneOS). Apps installed prior to the policy rollout will continue to work, though updating them requires completing one of the bypass routes. Turning off Developer Options after Advanced Flow setup will not revert permissions. Google’s plan to tighten the reins on Android sideloading has officially taken effect, with developer verification rules now rolling out across Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Certified Android devices running Google Play Services now actively block unverified app packages by default in these regions, with a wider global rollout on the cards for 2027. title: Android’s controversial new sideloading rules are officially here
summary: Google’s developer verification rules have reached their first Android users.
body: TL;DR Google’s new Android developer verification rules took effect on September 30 in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. Apps from participating stores must now come from verified developers before they can be installed on certified Android devices. Sideloading unregistered apps is still possible through Google’s new advanced flow, but it deliberately adds more friction. Android has always sold itself on one simple freedom that iPhone users don’t really get: the freedom to install whatever you want, from wherever you want. Google isn’t killing that freedom outright , but as of September 30, it has officially started putting a few more gates in the way — and Android users in four countries are the first through them. Google’s new developer verification rules are now in effect in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore, and Thailand. On certified devices running Android 7 or newer, apps installed through participating stores must be registered to a verified developer. The initial list includes Google Play, Galaxy Store, HONOR App Market, OPPO App Market, Xiaomi GetApps, vivo V-Appstore, and Transsion’s Palm Store.

title: A real ChatGPT page is being used to trick people into installing malware
summary: The dangerous part only appears after ChatGPT has already earned your trust.
body: TL;DR Attackers created a fake ChatGPT model called “Plus 5.6” on the real ChatGPT website. It sent users to a fake security check that tricked them into running a malicious Windows command. That command could install malware that could access files, the screen, the webcam, the microphone, and more. There was a time when spotting a sketchy download meant looking for misspelled websites, strange pop-ups, and other obvious red flags . But that gets much harder when the scam starts on a website you already trust. Security researchers have uncovered a malware campaign that does exactly that, using a real ChatGPT page to convince people they’re dealing with an official OpenAI product before redirecting them to a far more dangerous site. Researchers at Huntress (via TechRadar ) found attackers abusing ChatGPT’s Custom GPT feature to create a bot called “Plus 5.6.” The name was chosen to sound like an official OpenAI model, and because Custom GPTs are hosted on ChatGPT.com, anyone opening the link would see a legitimate ChatGPT address in their browser.

But every so often, a coincidence occurs: Two galaxies line up from our point of view on Earth (or from a space telescope) and appear to overlap in the sky. These rare overlapping galaxies give astronomers a chance to study something normally difficult to see: the dust inside one of these distant cosmic objects. That’s the focus of NASA’s new Overlap Zoo project. Picture the background galaxy acting like a cosmic flashlight, shining through the nearer galaxy. The backlit dust creates dark silhouettes, like shadows on a screen. By studying these silhouettes, astronomers can map how dust is distributed throughout galaxies and learn how it blocks, scatters, and dims starlight traveling through space.
